Name: Vein & Vine
Author: CinthyaBunny
Punchline: Priority-sorted gathering node tracker. No automation.
Description:
Shows a priority-sorted list of active and upcoming gathering nodes from your wishlist, using FFXIV's deterministic weather and Eorzea clock.

Read-only by design: it never moves your character and never gathers for you. The only action it takes is placing a map flag, which you still have to walk to.
Changelog:
Housekeeping release. No new features and no behaviour changes a player will notice, but the build now ships the artifact and the release notes it was supposed to all along.

Fixed:
- A release build produced two different latest.zip files. The solution mapped Debug|Any CPU twice per project with contradictory values, so the plugin built once to bin\x64\ and again, AnyCPU, to bin\. Both carried a packaged zip, 11 bytes apart, and nothing said which one was the real one — the exact failure NodeGen.csproj uses SetPlatform to avoid. The solution is now x64-only, which is all this plugin has ever targeted.
- The in-game installer has been showing no release notes at all. The build looked for a ## [version] heading that this file has never used, so the Changelog field in both manifests was left at whatever was last written by hand. The parser now keys off the bold version marker every entry carries, and reads the open newest entry and the collapsed older ones alike.
- repo.json declared AssemblyVersion as 0.0.1.3b, which is not a four-part version. The build's own guard only reads a four-part prefix, so it matched 0.0.1.3 and passed, while the changelog sync compared the whole string, disagreed, and skipped the file. Both now agree on 0.0.1.4.
- The main window discarded its own ImGui flags every frame. PreDraw assigned Flags from a helper that always returned None, so any flag set elsewhere would have been silently erased.
- Two different luminance formulas decided "is this a light theme?" One was correct WCAG with sRGB linearisation, the other inlined the same coefficients over raw values against a different threshold. All eight themes happen to agree under both, so nothing rendered differently, but the two could have diverged on any theme added later. There is now one test behind one constant.

Changed:
- Eight of sixteen injected Dalamud services were never used. Create<T>() resolves every [PluginService] property at construction, so each unused one was a hard dependency on a service surviving Dalamud's API surface — one renamed in a future API bump would have failed the whole plugin's load for something it never called.
- Dead and duplicated code removed: a no-op window-flags helper, three colour accessors that only forwarded to UiStyle, a table-flags block duplicated verbatim between the two lists, empty IDisposable implementations on both windows, and four unused members (GatherItem.Type, NodeQuery.MethodsFor, EorzeaTime.GetEorzeaMinute, EorzeaTime.TimeScale). TimeScale carried a warning about a rounding error that puts the Eorzea clock half a day out. The constant is gone; the warning moved to the constant that is actually used.
- Comments are now held to one rule, written down in CLAUDE.md: explain why, not what, and delete anything that restates the code. Roughly twenty-five doc comments went; the reasoning that records how the game's sheets actually behave stayed.
- Documentation that had drifted from the code was corrected rather than deleted. UiStyle still claimed to draw the game's WindowA panel art, removed back in 0.0.1.3; a comment asserted no ImGui tab bar is ever drawn, when docking the window makes ImGui draw one; the Appearance tab told players the window panel comes out of the client; and the README credited UiStyle with textures it no longer loads.

Notes:
- No change to the node dataset, the priority engine, or anything the plugin puts on screen. A player updating from 0.0.1.3b should see exactly what they saw before.
